plan.title: Liver treated vs control: descriptive DE, no replicates
plan.analytical_narrative: The data profile shows 1 treated and 1 control liver sample (12000 genes x 2 samples after metadata join, raw salmon-derived integer counts, no biological replication). With one sample per condition, DESeq2 cannot estimate within-group dispersion, so no inferential p-value has a valid basis (grounded rule R-0003). The plan therefore runs QC and normalization exactly as for any DESeq2 dataset, but stops short of a Wald test: it reports median-of-ratios normalized counts and apeglm-shrunken, descriptive log2 fold changes only, explicitly flagged as non-inferential. Because there is no p-value to threshold, gene selection for downstream interpretation uses a stated log2FC magnitude cutoff on the shrunken estimate, and enrichment runs as an over-representation test (not preranked GSEA, since GSEA also assumes a valid per-gene ranking statistic derived from an inferential model in the rule set for this design) against the tested-gene universe using the human MSigDB Hallmark and Reactome gene sets staged in this environment. The final report states plainly that this is a descriptive comparison of two individual samples, not a statistically tested differential expression result, and names the replicated design that would be needed for inference.
